checkpoints.description: Task 'keystone-wav-symmetry-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: fix the over-broad CLI catch-all that printed 'could not start' and blamed the game factory for every failure, including corrupt baseline reports and --diff-out size mismatches that happen long after the game loaded

impact_assessment.why: An agent following that Fix: advice would rewrite a working game module; the corrupt-baseline case also leaked a raw json decoder string.
impact_assessment.benefits: Post-start failures name something the caller can act on and are distinguishable from startup failures on the first line.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: error text changes for post-start failures; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the startup branch byte-identical, add _run_failure_hint chosen from the failing option, read comparison reports through a dedicated helper, and pin both branches with failing-first tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed - a started flag splits startup from post-start failures; post-start prints 'Keystone could not finish' plus per-option advice; comparison reports read through _read_comparison_report naming the file; 5 new tests, 2 fail against the pre-fix handler; 1005 tests; canonical hash unchanged; 6/6 gate; pushed 10c8a1d

[3/3] Additional probes found no defects: OBJ loader (triangulation, negative indices, 7 malformed rejections), asset_io (suffix inference, fingerprint), agents (observe, parse_actions, hash-chained AuditTrail with tamper detection, summarize_report), concurrency (atomic writes, concurrent readers, 60 concurrent editor creates, parallel library saves), CLI exit-code contract, and the full web API surface (11 malformed actions, non-object payloads, selected_ids semantics, lock enforcement on 5 mutating paths, undo/redo bounds); confirmed ADR-063 report-hash behaviour is intentional and the pixel gate uses same_image; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-cli-advice-v1' completed successfully.
[1/2] Plan: digit key names, dead-key diagnostics and input_keys in --describe, driven by the shooter testbed

impact_assessment.why: The shooter testbed could not bind weapon slots: the real key table had no number row, and bind() accepted dead names such as mouse_left without telling the consumer.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games can bind the number row, and a declared button with no working key is visible through Engine.unbound_buttons/unknown_keys and --describe.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: public input surface; dependency: glfw key constants (already required); concurrency: none; state: context.py, input.py, app.py, plugin.py, tests, README, CHANGELOG
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first key-table and diagnostic tests, existing bind-hook tests, full suite and 6/6 gates

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Digit keys + dead-key diagnostics verified: 942 tests, 6/6 gates (test, lint, mechanics, hygiene, guidelines, secrets)
Task 'keystone-input-keys-diagnostics' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: the unpushed 3c84b49 added a tracked tests/test_input_keys.py but omitted it from the README directory tree, so check --strict failed the guidelines gate with PRINCIPLE-005 R5 while the other five gates passed

impact_assessment.why: The tree check is the only gate that compares the filesystem to the README, so a missing entry blocks delivery even though every test is green.
impact_assessment.benefits: Strict check and delivery work again, and a cold-starting agent can find the new test file from the README.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none (documentation only); dependency: none; concurrency: the tree may be edited concurrently; state: README char budget.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add one tree line, re-run update_knowledge_base --check, verify no merged bullets or unbalanced fences, and keep well under 32,500 chars.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed and pushed - README lists test_input_keys.py, guidelines gate reports size/labels/tree/commands OK, README 31,143 chars, 6/6 strict gates pass, pushed 3c84b49 and c4c01da

[3/3] Additional probes found no defects: canvas alignment (text_right lands exactly on the margin, text_center symmetric, truncation never overflows, line height linear, degenerate sizes rejected) and the live HTTP surface (four GET endpoints, 404 with error+fix JSON, 405 on wrong method, 400 on malformed JSON, 413 at the 1,000,000-byte body limit with the server still healthy, CORS present, /api/editor action round-trip over HTTP, clean shutdown); checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-readme-tree-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: fix the frame-report node bbox, which dropped corners behind the near plane so the sample floor collapsed to a zero-height line at the horizon even though it fills the lower 56% of the rendered frame

impact_assessment.why: The project goal is vision-model analyzability; a bbox that contradicts the image is worse than no bbox.
impact_assessment.benefits: An AI reading the report localises ground planes and any surface crossing the camera correctly.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: bbox values change for near-plane-crossing meshes; dependency: none; concurrency: outer toolkit is being edited in parallel; state: report schema stays 11.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Clip box edges at the near plane z+w==0 (not w==0, which is the eye and divides by zero), clamp to the frame, keep schema 11, and pin the floor plus identity-matrix cases with failing-first tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed and verified - _projected_bbox clips the twelve box edges against the near plane and clamps to the frame; floor now [0.0, 27.81, 96.0, 64.0] matching the render; 1022 tests pass; canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde unchanged; reference PNG 4899B; 6/6 gates pass

[3/3] Visual confirmation - rendered the sample scene and read the image: the checkered floor fills the bottom half from the horizon down, matching the new bbox; schema note documents the clamping rule; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-bbox-nearclip-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: fix the --project load-failure advice, which told the caller to pass a package.module:Factory even though --project derives the spec from keystone.json, so renaming the scaffolded Game class produced unactionable guidance

impact_assessment.why: AI-driven game creation is a stated project goal; a misleading Fix: during the authoring loop sends an agent to edit the wrong thing.
impact_assessment.benefits: An AI that refactors its entry class is pointed at the one field that needs updating and can verify recovery immediately.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: startup error text changes when --project is set; dependency: none; concurrency: outer toolkit still being edited; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add _start_failure_hint keyed on args.project, keep the factory text for explicit --game, and pin scaffold-rename-recover as a failing-first test.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed and verified - _start_failure_hint names the keystone.json game field under --project and keeps the factory advice for explicit --game; scaffold-rename-recover test fails against the pre-fix handler; 1023 tests pass; 6/6 gates pass

[3/3] Authoring-loop walk confirms the rest of the path is sound: --new scaffolds a validated project that simulates and renders as shipped, an edit re-validates and re-simulates, and the headless report shows the edited node with its bbox; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-project-start-hint-v1' completed successfully.
